newsitem.title: USA: Texas water board presents $100 mln bond proposal.
newsitem.headline: Texas water board presents $100 mln bond proposal.

text.p: The Texas Water Development Board on Tuesday presented a proposed $100 million negotiated general obligation bond to the state's bond review board for approval.

"It is a negotiated transaction with Bank One Capital Corp as lead manager," said Nancy Marstiller, the water board's debt issue manager. "We hope to get approval by July 17 and anticipate the sale in the week of July 28."
She said $75 million of the $100 million would go into the board's water supply account for providing loans to communities for water projects. That chunk would be for 20 years, maturing in 2019.

The remaining $25 million, for 21 years maturing in 2020, would be set aside for the "Economically Distressed Areas" along Texas' border with Mexico. Marstiller said it would be used for loans to build much-needed water and sewer facilities.
She said the exact sale date will depend on market activity during the week of July 28.

"If I can get 5.25 (coupon or interest rate) or less, I will be happy," she said. "We'll be applying to all three rating agencies to have the ratings a week before the pricing. We expect the same rating as for the whole state, which is 'Double A'."
Co-managers of the bond program are Artemis Capital Group, Bear Stearns & Co., Legg Mason Wood Walker Inc. and Walton Johnson & Co.

The cost of the bond sale is projected at $8.05 per $1,000 face value for a total cost of $805,000. "The review board will look at the cost closely and we are hoping it will be less than $8.05," Marstiller said.
The water board's last bond sale was for $95 million in December 1996.
